planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; unlike single-stem seed sunflowers, Sunbelievable is a vegetatively propagated, sterile hybrid that branches continuously and never needs deadheading or staking for a single giant bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after the last frost, and expect a mounded, heavily branching plant rather than the tall single stalk of a traditional sunflower. Sunbelievable is a sterile hybrid sunflower series bred for nonstop bloom, covering itself in hundreds of small, 2-inch, brown-eyed golden flowers continuously from late spring until frost without ever needing deadheading, since sterile flowers do not go to seed and stop blooming the way fertile sunflowers do. Its dense, self-branching, weather-resistant habit holds up well in wind and rain without staking, making it a reliable choice for containers, borders, and mass plantings where a traditional sunflower's single giant bloom and floppy stem would be impractical. Because it is a sterile hybrid, it is propagated only from cuttings and sold as a rooted plant rather than from seed.
sources: Proven Winners — Sunbelievable sunflower series notes

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; Vermillionaire is a sterile hybrid propagated by cuttings, sold as a rooted plant, and blooms nonstop through summer heat without setting seed.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, and feed regularly through the growing season to fuel its continuous bloom. Vermillionaire is a sterile hybrid cuphea bred as a non-invasive, seedless alternative to the older, self-seeding cigar plant, producing an even heavier, nonstop display of small, tubular, bright orange flowers on a well-branched, mounding plant that draws hummingbirds from the moment it opens its first flowers until frost. Because it never sets seed, it does not spread or naturalize the way older cigar-flower cuphea can, making it a better-behaved choice for borders, mixed containers, and pollinator gardens. It is winter hardy only in the warmest zones and is typically grown as a summer annual elsewhere, propagated from cuttings taken before frost to overwinter indoors.
sources: Proven Winners — Vermillionaire cuphea variety notes

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Angelface was bred for larger flowers and a more compact, uniform habit than seed-grown angelonia, and it thrives in the heat and humidity of Gulf South summers when most other bedding annuals fade.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after the last frost, and expect vigorous, heat-proof performance right through the hottest, most humid stretch of summer when many bedding plants stall. Angelface is a vegetatively propagated angelonia series bred for notably larger, snapdragon-like flower spikes and a denser, more uniform mounding habit than older seed-grown angelonia, blooming continuously from spring through frost in shades of blue, purple, pink, and white without deadheading. Its exceptional heat and humidity tolerance, along with resistance to the diseases that trouble many summer annuals in wet conditions, has made it one of the most reliable performers for Gulf South beds, borders, and containers through the peak of summer. Pinch young plants once to encourage bushier growth, and feed regularly through the season to sustain the heavy bloom.
sources: Proven Winners — Angelface angelonia series notes

common_name: Bandana Lantana (Compact Mounding Landscape Lantana Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; Bandana was bred for a compact, uniform mounding habit that stays tidier than older seed-grown lantana, making it well suited to mass plantings and containers as well as beds.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun, and avoid overwatering, since lantana is highly drought-tolerant once established and prone to root problems in soggy soil. Bandana is a vegetatively propagated landscape lantana series bred for a compact, dense, mounding habit and a wide range of vivid multicolor flower clusters that shift shades as they age, blooming nonstop from spring through frost and drawing butterflies heavily throughout the season. Its uniform size and tidy growth make it more predictable for mass landscape plantings than older seed-grown lantana cultivars, which can vary in vigor and habit, while retaining the same outstanding heat and drought tolerance the species is known for. In the coldest parts of its hardiness range it dies to the ground in winter and returns from the roots in spring; further north it is grown as a summer annual.
sources: Proven Winners — Bandana lantana series notes

common_name: Truffula Pink Gomphrena (Tall Wand-Form Globe Amaranth)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Truffula Pink thrives in the heat and humidity of Gulf South summers, holding up better than many annuals during the peak of the season.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun, and expect minimal maintenance beyond routine watering, since gomphrena is highly heat- and drought-tolerant once established. Truffula Pink is a tall, vigorous gomphrena selection producing an abundance of rounded, papery, bright pink flower globes held well above the foliage on long, airy stems, creating a wand-like effect that stands out in a border or cutting garden and gives the plant its whimsical name. The flowers hold their color exceptionally well both in the garden and after cutting, making Truffula Pink a favorite for fresh and dried arrangements, and its nonstop bloom from summer through frost provides reliable color when many other annuals falter in Gulf South heat. It is also highly attractive to butterflies and other pollinators throughout its long bloom season. Deadheading is not required for continued bloom, though removing spent stems keeps the planting tidy.
sources: Proven Winners — Truffula gomphrena series notes
